options.text: Let's see your stock.
Show me what you're selling.
I'm here to buy.
Open the ledger. What have you got?
I've got coin and a long shopping list.
Time to spend some emeralds.
What's on the shelves today?
Let's do business, quartermaster.
I need supplies. Sell me some.
Lay it all out. I'm buying.
Got anything to sell me?
Can I buy some gear off you?
How much for that bread you're carrying?
Would you part with your spare rations?
I'll pay good coin for supplies. Interested?
You look like someone with things to trade.
Any chance you'd sell some of that kit?
Who do I talk to if I want to buy something?
What kind of goods does your side deal in?
What do soldiers like you usually sell?
Is there a market in this camp?
Tell me about your supply lines.
Do you sell to outsiders?
What's worth buying around here?
I hear armies always have surplus. True?
What passes for a shop out here?
What is your side short on?
What supplies do you need most?
If I brought you materials, would you pay?
What's scarce out here?
What would make your lives easier? I can haul.
Tell me what the front needs. I'll fetch it.
I want to keep you all supplied. What's the list?
Name what you're missing and consider it found.
That price seems steep.
Can you do better on the price?
I've seen this cheaper elsewhere.
Knock a little off and we have a deal.
Do you ever haggle, or is the price the price?
Would you take goods instead of emeralds?
What if I bought in bulk?
Let's negotiate. I'm patient.
Come on, surely friends get to haggle.
For a loyal customer, you could round that down.
Here — fresh bread, four loaves. On me.
Take this bread for the mess. No charge.
I baked too much. Have some loaves.
A little bread for the watch tonight.
Four iron ingots. A gift for your smiths.
Take this iron. Patch your armor.
Some spare iron for the forge. Keep it.
Iron ingots, free of charge. Put them to use.
Here's leather for boots. A gift.
Take these hides. Your straps look worn.
Some leather for repairs. No payment needed.
I tanned extra leather. It's yours.
Two emeralds for the unit fund. A gift.
Take a couple of emeralds. Call it goodwill.
Emeralds, no strings. Buy the squad something.
A small gift of gems, from me to your people.
Why is everything double for me?
These prices are robbery.
You're gouging me on purpose, aren't you?
Is this what everyone pays, or just me?
That's three times what it's worth.
How do I get an honest price around here?
Your rates got steeper since last time.
Do I get charged extra for breathing too?
What would this cost someone you liked?
I can't be the only one you charge like this.
Come on, meet me halfway on the cost.
I'll pay a fair rate, not a punishment rate.
Lower the price and I'll forget the insult.
You'd rather gouge me than make a sale?
Even bandits leave a man his boots.
Every coin I have and it's still not enough?
Fine. Name a number that isn't spite.
Will you even sell to me anymore?
Am I banned from the market, then?
Is my coin no good here?
Can we still do business, after everything?
I'm not here for trouble. Just trade.
Look, commerce doesn't care about grudges.
You need customers. I need supplies. Simple.
Whatever you think of me, my emeralds spend.
Any friendly rates for me today?
Do friends of yours shop cheaper?
What's the discount for good company?
Surely my record here is worth a few emeralds off.
I keep coming back. That loyalty worth anything?
Give me the price you'd give one of your own.
Sharpen that price for an old friend.
You know I'm good for it. Trim the cost.
Got anything you don't show strangers?
What's in the back, behind the crates?
Any special stock for trusted customers?
Show me the good stuff, not the surplus.
I hear quartermasters keep the best hidden.
What would you sell only to a friend?
Anything rare come through lately?
Is your gear actually any good?
How does your kit hold up in a fight?
Who makes your equipment?
Would you trust your own stock with your life?
What's the best-made thing you carry?
Does anything you sell come with a guarantee?

negative: Fine. Coin first, complaints never. Touch nothing you can't pay for.
The crates are open. My eyes are too.
We sell to you because supply doesn't care. Don't make me care.
neutral: Surplus is what survives the front. Take your pick.
Crates on the left survived the winter. Start there.
Buy something or make room for someone who will.
positive: For you? The good crates. The ones we don't show the inspectors.
Come, friend. The line eats first, but you eat second.
Take a look. Prices soft as spring mud today.

negative: Transaction authorized. Barely. All sales are final and on the record.
You may purchase. You may not linger. Manifest is posted.
The supply window is open. Your file stays open with it.
neutral: Manifest is current as of this morning. Name what you need.
Approved goods only. Payment on receipt. Proceed.
Stores are open. Queue is you. Go ahead.
positive: Cleared for the full manifest, friend. Including the second page.
Good timing — resupply landed at dawn. Take your pick.
For you the window stays open past hours. What do you need?

negative: The cloth comes off the wares, but my hand stays near the knife. Browse.
Buy quickly. Hospitality has hours, and yours are short.
Even a salted well sells water to the desperate. Look, then.
neutral: Sit. What is under the cloth is for sale. What is under the sand is not.
The caravan was kind this month. See what it left.
Look with your eyes first. Hands are a later privilege.
positive: For you the cloth comes all the way off. Even the corner pile.
The best of the caravan waits for friends. It has waited for you.
Choose slowly. The shade is free and so is my patience today.

negative: I dig and I hold. I don't sell. And to you I wouldn't even dig.
My kit is the line's kit. Ask the quartermaster, if he'll have you.
neutral: Not my crates. Quartermaster handles trade. I handle mud.
You want the quartermaster. Fat tent, thin patience.
positive: Ha, if I sold my boots I'd die barefoot. Quartermaster's tent, friend.
Everything I own is on my back and half is the army's. See the quartermaster.

negative: Negative. Sales go through supply, and supply reads the flag on your file.
I am not authorized to trade. You are barely authorized to be here.
neutral: Trade runs through the quartermaster. Follow the crates.
Not my lane. Supply handles transactions.
positive: Wish I could help, but supply owns the ledgers. Quartermaster's that way, friend.
Above my pay grade to sell you anything. Supply will sort you out.

negative: A scorpion does not carry a purse. Ask the keeper of wares, if you must.
I hold nothing you can buy, and trust nothing you can offer.
neutral: The one who keeps the wares sits by the water. I only keep watch.
My hands carry a blade, not a scale. Seek the merchant of the camp.
positive: If it were mine, friend, it would be yours. It is not. The keeper of wares will smile at you.
I own my shadow and my patience. For goods, seek the one with the carpets.

negative: We deal in what winters leave behind. None of it is for you at kind prices.
Surplus, salvage, spite. Guess which one you get.
neutral: Boots, timber, iron, bread. Army things. Nothing pretty, everything tested.
Whatever survives the front twice gets sold once.
positive: For friends? Tools, iron, warm things. The line shares what it can spare.
Rations that don't crawl, blades that don't bend. Best market in the mud.

negative: Approved surplus only. The interesting stock needs clearance you will never hold.
There is a market. Your access to it is under review.
neutral: Surplus rotation covers hardware, textiles, field provisions. All logged.
Supply sells decommissioned stock on schedule. Quartermaster posts the list.
positive: Between rotations we clear good hardware. Friends hear about it first.
The manifest is dull, but the margins are honest. Ask supply for the fresh page.

negative: We sell shade to the sun-struck and rope to the drowning. What do you drown in?
The market is a well. Some are welcome to drink. Some are the reason it is guarded.
neutral: Cloth, water, dates, patience. The caravan brings the rest when it pleases.
What the dunes swallow, we sometimes sell back. Ask the keeper of wares.
positive: For friends the caravan has a longer memory and a deeper bag.
We trade what the desert gives: hides, salt, secrets. The first two have prices.

negative: We need nothing a debtor carries.
The line needs bodies and bread. You've cost us one. Start with the other.
neutral: Bread, iron, leather. The front eats all three.
Timber for the trench, grain for the pot. Always. Forever.
positive: Iron, friend. The line chews through iron like black bread.
Bring boots or bring bread. Either makes you family.

negative: Deliveries from you require vetting. Deliver first. Trust maybe later.
The list exists. Your name is not cleared to read it.
neutral: Current shortfalls: iron stock, cured leather, field rations. Fair rates on delivery.
Supply posts its shortfalls weekly. Iron and provisions top the sheet.
positive: Off the record: lens-grade glass and good leather. Bring either and supply will smile.
Iron before winter, friend. Deliver and the ledger remembers.

negative: We need the debt paid. After that, ask again.
From you? Distance. Bring us distance.
neutral: Water finds us. String, cloth, and iron must be found. Bring those.
The desert provides patience. Everything else, the caravan buys.
positive: Bring string for the snares and cloth for the night, friend. The camp will bless your name.
What we lack is small and light: string, salt, good thread. Carry some and be doubly welcome.

negative: The price is the price, and for you it grows when you argue.
Haggle harder and I add a grief tax.
neutral: Everything costs what it costs. The war did the negotiating already.
You can haggle with me or with winter. I'm the softer one, barely.
positive: Ha! For you I pretend to argue, then I give the real price. Done.
You bargain like a supply sergeant. Fine, fine — a little off the top.

negative: Rates are fixed and your discount is revoked. Next item.
Negotiation denied. Pricing reflects risk. You are the risk.
neutral: Pricing is set by supply, not sentiment. I can note your objection.
The rate card is posted. I don't argue with laminate.
positive: For a known friendly I can apply the field adjustment. Quietly.
I'll round in your favor and call it a rounding error. Once.

negative: You bargain like a man buying his own rope. The price holds.
Haggling is a dance. You have stepped on too many feet to dance here.
neutral: Every price in the desert is a conversation. Sit, and we will converse.
The first price is for strangers. Stay long enough to hear the second.
positive: Ah, you know the game. For friends, the third price — the true one.
For you we skip the theater. Here is the friend's number.

negative: Bread from your hands. The pot doesn't ask where flour came from. We'll count it anyway.
The mess takes it. The ledger notes it. Nothing is forgiven for loaves, but nothing is wasted either.
neutral: Bread is bread. The pot thanks you, and the pot speaks for all of us.
Warm loaves at the front. Someone pinch me.
positive: Fresh bread and a friendly face. Today the line eats like officers.
You feed the line, the line remembers your plate. Sit, tear a piece with us.

negative: Provisions accepted and inspected. Goodwill noted, trust pending.
Donation logged. It buys calories, not clearance.
neutral: Provisions received. Entered in the ledger as goodwill. Appreciated.
The mess sergeant will be pleased. Logged and thanks.
positive: Fresh bread beats field crackers every deployment. The unit thanks you, friend.
Donation received with actual enthusiasm. Rare event. Noted twice.

negative: Bread offered by a shadowed hand. We eat it in daylight and remember the hand.
The camp accepts the loaf. The debt sits apart from it, untouched.
neutral: Bread shared on the road is a small treaty. The camp accepts.
You give, we receive, the desert witnesses. Kindly done.
positive: Warm bread from a warm hand. The tents will speak your name at supper.
A guest who brings bread is halfway to family. Sit, eat your own gift with us.

negative: Iron from you. The forge doesn't care. The forge is smarter than we are.
We'll beat it into wire and spikes. Your gift will guard the trench against you if it must.
neutral: Good iron. The smith will stop complaining for one hour. A record.
Iron for the line. Practical. We respect practical.
positive: Iron! Now this is a gift, friend. The smith may even smile. Don't stare — it frightens him.
The line runs on iron and stubbornness. You just doubled our supply of one.

negative: Materiel accepted into stores. This changes inventory, not your file.
Iron logged in receiving. Motive logged elsewhere.
neutral: Iron stock received and weighed. Supply appreciates accurate donations.
Four ingots into stores. The armorer says thank you. I'm paraphrasing.
positive: Quality ingots, friend. The armorer owes you a fitting now.
Iron on hand means bolts in racks. Solid contribution. Logged with a star.

negative: Iron from your hand. We will make hooks of it and hope they never need your name.
The forge takes all metal, even metal with a history.
neutral: Iron is rare as rain here. The camp accepts with both hands.
Metal given freely cuts deeper than metal sold. In the good way. Our thanks.
positive: Iron for the smiths of the sand. Your name will ring on the anvil, friend.
You bring the desert what it cannot grow. That is remembered longest.

negative: Hides from you. Boots don't ask who tanned them. Lucky boots.
Leather taken. Winter doesn't check the giver's ledger, so we won't today either.
neutral: Leather. Straps, boots, patience. All three wear out here. Thanks.
The cobbler will drink to your health. He drinks to everything, but still.
positive: Good hides, friend! Half the line walks on hope and rag. Not this month.
Leather from a friend keeps feet dry and grudges away. The line thanks you.

negative: Cured hides accepted into stores. Goodwill entry: provisional.
Leather received. Trust is a different material.
neutral: Hides logged into supply. The riggers needed these. Acknowledged.
Leather received in fair condition. Entered as donation. Thank you.
positive: The riggers have been splicing scraps for weeks. You just made their month, friend.
Prime hides. Supply will sing. Off-key, but sincerely.

negative: Hides from a hard hand. The desert cures all leather and some men. We accept.
We take the gift. The sand takes note.
neutral: Leather travels well and lies little. The camp thanks you.
Good hides. The saddler will bless a stranger tonight.
positive: Soft hides from a soft-hearted friend. The tents will wear your kindness.
Leather for the straps, friendship for the road. Both hold. Our thanks.

negative: Emeralds. The line can't eat them, but the ledger enjoys the shine.
Green stones from a red ledger. We take them. The count continues.
neutral: Emeralds for the fund. The men vote vodka. The sergeant votes socks. Socks will win.
Shiny. Useful. Accepted. Three words, all true.
positive: Emeralds from a friend! Tonight the line toasts you with the good water.
Green stones, warm gesture. The fund grows and so does your name here.

negative: Currency accepted into the unit fund. This is a receipt, not a thaw.
Emeralds logged. Generosity noted, provenance assumed complicated.
neutral: Contribution entered into the unit fund. Correct and appreciated.
Two emeralds, unit fund, logged. Efficient generosity. My favorite kind.
positive: Into the fund, friend. The mess gets real coffee this month because of you.
Generous, with zero strings attached. You're becoming my favorite civilian.

negative: Green stones catch the light. So do knives. We accept the first and keep the second close.
The gift enters the tent. The giver waits outside a while longer.
neutral: Emeralds shine like water at dusk. The camp accepts your kindness.
Two green stones, freely given. The desert notices what is done without asking.
positive: Gems from a friend gleam twice. Once in the hand, once in the telling.
The camp will trade these for what the sand cannot give. Your kindness travels far, friend.

negative: Double? Count again. For you it's triple. Arithmetic is our love language.
You pay the grief rate. Every name on it is one of ours.
The price of goods is low. The price of forgetting is high. You're buying both.
neutral: Fair is a place, not a price. But fine, the number can breathe a little.
Everyone pays the war tax. You just notice it more.
positive: Gouge a friend? Never. Overcharge one gently? Only on Tuesdays.
Relax. For you the scale is honest and the thumb stays off it.

negative: Pricing includes a risk surcharge. You are the risk. It's itemized.
The rate reflects your file. Improve the file, improve the rate.
Complaint noted, filed, and priced in.
neutral: Rates are uniform. Perception of unfairness is not an invoice error.
The margin covers convoy losses. Argue with the ambushes, not with me.
positive: You're on the friendly rate already. It goes lower only if you enlist.
Check the card again, friend. You're paying less than my own captain.

negative: The thirsty pay in coin. The unwelcome pay in coin and apology. You count only the coin.
Salt your neighbor's well and even water costs like honey.
The number offends you? It carries your history in it. History is heavy.
neutral: Prices drift like dunes. Today the wind is against you. Tomorrow, who knows.
The souk has moods. Argue sweetly and it may soften.
positive: For you the price sheds its cloak. See? Smaller underneath.
A friend pays the true number. Strangers subsidize your tea.

negative: Your coin spends. Your welcome doesn't. Buy fast.
We sell to you like we shovel in the rain. Necessary, joyless, quick.
Business, yes. Trust, no. Hands where the sentry likes them.
neutral: Nobody banned you. The market has no feelings. The people around it do.
Trade is trade. Just don't expect the tea.
positive: Banned? Friend, we'd sooner ban bread. Come, buy, gossip.
The market loves you like the quota loves numbers. Deeply.

negative: Commerce with flagged individuals is permitted under supervision. You are supervised.
Your currency clears. Your reputation does not. Transactions only.
You may trade. Terms: cash, daylight, witnesses.
neutral: No restriction on record. Normal terms apply.
You're cleared for commerce. Everything else is a separate form.
positive: Restricted? You're practically on the vendor list, friend.
Your account's in good order. Better than most enlisted, honestly.

negative: We trade with the storm too, when it leaves us no choice. Wait in the doorway. Do not come in.
Your coin is welcome the way rain is welcome in the flood.
Buy what you need. Need nothing twice.
neutral: The market refuses no one with clean hands and quick feet.
Trade is older than grudges. Older, not stronger. Mind both.
positive: The stalls open for you like morning, friend. Who told you otherwise?
Coin from your hand is doubly good. It arrives with a smile.

negative: A discount? You owe more than the shelf is worth.
The friendly rate died with our friends. Full price.
neutral: Discounts are for the line. Sleep in enough mud and we'll talk.
The loyalty rate exists. Yours is still being earned. Come back with history.
positive: For you, the soldier's price. Don't tell the soldiers — they pay more.
Ha, the friend of the line pays like family. Grumbling included, free.

negative: Preferred pricing requires preferred status. You are the opposite of preferred.
Discount denied. Your ledger is in arrears where it counts.
neutral: Adjustments require documented service to this command. Bring documentation.
The rate card has one tier for civilians. You're on it.
positive: Applying the allied rate, friend. Signed, stamped, slightly illegal.
Loyalty documented, discount applied. The system works occasionally.

negative: Kind prices grow from kind soil. You planted salt.
First mend the well. Then ask the water to be cheap.
neutral: The friend's price is real. So is the road that leads to it. Walk it.
Generosity is a harvest. Sow a season first.
positive: For you the price bows, friend. It has heard about you from the fire.
Take the friend's number and tell no one. Envy sours tea.

negative: The back room? For you the front room is a courtesy.
The good crates hide from people like you. Smart crates.
neutral: Special stock goes to special names. Yours is still ordinary ink.
What's in the back is spoken for. By people who bled for it.
positive: Come around the crates. What the inspectors don't see keeps morale alive.
For the line's friend? There's a box under the box. Look twice.

negative: Restricted inventory stays restricted. Asking is itself noted.
There is no back shelf. Officially. For you, also actually.
neutral: Non-standard stock needs authorization above mine. And above yours.
The interesting shelf exists behind paperwork. Thick paperwork.
positive: Between us: a crate fell off a manifest. Undamaged. Interested?
For cleared friends the second manifest exists. Read fast, it's shy.

negative: What is hidden is hidden from someone. Today, from you.
The best wares sleep. Your voice would wake them badly.
neutral: Everything has a beneath. Beneath is earned, not sold.
The caravan keeps its pearls for faces it has seen thrice.
positive: Lean close, friend. Under the third carpet — things the sun has never priced.
The hidden shelf knows your name now. Ask it sweetly.

negative: Good enough to outlive you. That's the only warranty here.
Our gear survives winters. Whether you do is your business.
neutral: Nothing shines. Everything works. That's the Vostok promise.
Tested by mud, approved by mud. Mud is honest.
positive: The gear is ugly, friend, and it will never, ever quit on you. Like us.
Every blade here has an opinion and a body count. Good steel.

negative: Our equipment meets spec. Discussion of spec is not available to you.
Quality assured. Buyer scrutiny logged.
neutral: All stock passes inspection twice. Once by regs, once by sergeants. The sergeants are stricter.
Materiel is rated, tagged, and traceable. Failures get autopsies.
positive: Honest answer, friend? The export table is fine. The unit table is better. You're now export-plus.
I stake my cert on every item here. The cert took me six years.

negative: Our goods endure the desert. The desert endures everything. Draw your conclusions.
Quality is proven in silence, not promised in speech. Buy or don't.
neutral: The desert eats the flimsy first. What we sell, it hasn't eaten.
Ask the dunes how our rope holds. They have tested every span.
positive: For you I will say what the seller never says: this piece — yes. That one — walk past.
The good thread sings when you pull it. Here — listen, friend.
